subject.title: [Feature]: Skill lifecycle management — auto-optimization on failure + usage-based retirement

question: Should OpenClaw add core skill lifecycle management for outcome-based repair proposals and usage-based archive/retirement, or should this stay in plugin/ClawHub design until a missing core API is identified?
rationale: The remaining request adds new config, persistent skill/session state, ranking behavior, and potential deletion semantics; automation cannot choose the consent and core-versus-plugin boundary safely.

options.title: Design Core Lifecycle API First
options.body: Define the persisted metrics, user approval rules, and Skill Workshop proposal provenance before any implementation PR.

options.title: Route To Plugin/ClawHub Extension
options.body: Keep core lean and require a plugin API proposal only if current extension points cannot implement lifecycle scoring safely.

options.title: Close As Not Planned
options.body: Decline automated retirement or optimization if maintainers do not want OpenClaw to infer skill edits or lifecycle actions from usage data.

recommendation.title: Design Core Lifecycle API First
recommendation.body: Define the persisted metrics, user approval rules, and Skill Workshop proposal provenance before any implementation PR.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent authored the current reactive-correction capture change that partially overlaps the request and is the strongest current-main routing signal.
